Name: Virtue Ethics / Eudaimonism
Description: Ethics centered on the cultivation of good character and the virtues needed for human flourishing (eudaimonia).

Name: Civic / Communitarian Ethics
Description: Ethics centered on civic duty, the common good, and the individual's obligations to community and polity.

Name: No Systematic Ethics
Description: Philosophers who did not develop, or are not primarily known for, a systematic ethical theory.

Name: Existentialist Ethics
Description: Ethics centered on individual freedom, authenticity, and the self-creation of one's own values.

Name: Christian / Divine Command Ethics
Description: Ethics grounded in Christian revelation, divine command, grace, and the imitation of Christ.

Name: Buddhist / Hindu / Jain Ethics
Description: Ethics centered on compassion, non-violence, and liberation from suffering as developed in Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain traditions.

Name: Deontology / Rights-based Ethics
Description: Ethics centered on duty, moral rules, and individual rights rather than consequences or character.

Name: Socialist / Emancipatory Ethics
Description: Ethics centered on class emancipation, liberation from oppression, and the critique of exploitative social structures.

Name: Consequentialism / Utilitarianism
Description: Ethics that judges actions by their outcomes, especially the overall balance of happiness or well-being they produce.

Name: Discourse / Recognition Ethics
Description: Ethics grounded in mutual recognition, communicative rationality, and norms justified through open discourse.

Name: Confucian / Daoist Ethics
Description: Ethics centered on ritual propriety, role-based relationships, or natural spontaneity as developed in Confucian and Daoist thought.

Name: Stoic / Contemplative Ethics
Description: Ethics centered on inner tranquility, self-mastery, and living in accordance with nature or reason.

Name: Anti-colonial / Solidarity Ethics
Description: Ethics centered on liberation from colonial and racial oppression and solidarity among the oppressed.

Name: Feminist / Care Ethics
Description: Ethics centered on care, relationality, and the critique of gender inequality in traditional moral theory.

Name: Islamic Ethics
Description: Ethics grounded in Islamic revelation, law, and the cultivation of virtue within an Islamic framework.
